task_title: validate output: 535 warnings overwhelm new users
task_criteria: node bin/speclang validate exits 0 and its output contains Warnings: followed by a numeric warning count without flooding the user with hundreds of raw warning lines; npx vitest run tests/validation/engine.test.ts tests/validation/rules.test.ts exits 0 with all 33 tests passing; npm run build exits 0.

items.criterion: node bin/speclang validate exits 0 and its output contains Warnings: followed by a numeric warning count without flooding the user with hundreds of raw warning lines; npx vitest run tests/validation/engine.test.ts tests/validation/rules.test.ts exits 0 with all 33 tests passing; npm run build exits 0.
items.detail: Ran `node bin/speclang validate` in /home/kara/SpecLang: EXIT=0, stdout is 20 lines total (stderr empty). It contains `  Warnings: 535` (line 8) followed by a compact breakdown (`Warnings by rule (94 of 452 files): @validation/autonomous 532 / @validation/header 3`, top-5 messages, `… 156 more distinct warning(s)`, and a `--verbose` / `--format json` hint) — no per-file blocks and no raw `⚠ [rule]` warning lines. Implementation: specs/validation.spec.dir/src/cli.ts:130-140 prints a per-file block only when `verbose || report.errors.length > 0`, and cli.ts:174-180 appends `reporter.formatWarningSummary(reports)`; the summary itself is specs/validation.spec.dir/src/reporter.ts:98-160. `npx vitest run tests/validation/engine.test.ts tests/validation/rules.test.ts` → EXIT=0, `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  33 passed (33)`. `npm run build` (tsc) → EXIT=0 with no diagnostics; read_lsp_diagnostics returned 0 findings. Regression coverage tests/validation/validate-output.test.ts also passes 9/9 (whole tests/validation/ dir: 4 files, 45 tests passed, EXIT=0). [resolution 0.13; tests/validation/engine.test.ts, tests/validation/rules.test.ts]

items.criterion: The summarized output is reachable from the real CLI entrypoint (bin/speclang validate), not just from the library function.
items.detail: bin/speclang:596 `const { validateCommand } = require('../dist/src/validation/cli.js')` and :597-604 call it with the parsed options; the built artifact dist/src/validation/cli.js is regenerated by `npm run build` (EXIT=0) and dist/src/validation/reporter.js:74 contains `formatWarningSummary`. Running the binary produced the 20-line summary, and `node bin/speclang check` (bin/speclang:667, same validateCommand) also produced 20 lines with `Warnings: 535` at line 8 — so both user-facing entrypoints reach the new behaviour.

items.criterion: `--verbose` still restores full per-file/per-warning detail (detail on demand, not lost).
items.detail: `node bin/speclang validate --verbose` → EXIT=0, 2991 lines, per-warning lines such as `⚠ [@validation/autonomous] 23: Potentially ambiguous language: "etc."` (line 19) and `1 warning(s)` per-file headers, with the summary at line 2980 (`Warnings: 535`). Pinned by tests/validation/validate-output.test.ts "--verbose restores per-file detail and every warning" (passing).

items.criterion: `--format json` remains a machine contract: valid JSON on stdout, unchanged fields, no human summary text.
items.detail: `node bin/speclang validate --format json` → EXIT=0; stdout parses as JSON (`json ok 452 535 452` — totalFiles 452, warnings 535, reports length 452) and contains no `Warnings by rule` text; the banner goes to stderr (bin/speclang:589-591). Pinned by the "--format json keeps stdout machine-readable" test (passing).

items.criterion: Exit-code semantics are preserved: warnings alone do not fail the run, and `--strict` still promotes them to errors.
items.detail: Default run: EXIT=0 with 535 warnings (cli.ts:150 `success: totalErrors === 0 && uniqueFiles.length > 0`). `node bin/speclang validate --strict` → EXIT=1 with `Failed: 94`, `Errors: 535`, `Warnings: 0`, i.e. warnings were promoted exactly as before the change.
